summary: DARK SPACE is an interactive web platform designed to bring astronomy closer to students and people interested in the universe. Our project allows users to explore stars, galaxies, constellations, and different regions of space through images and visual tools. It also aims to make NASA's SPHEREx mission data easier to understand by displaying infrared images and allowing users to compare observations from different dates to identify possible moving objects. Our goal is to transform complex astronomical information into a simple, dynamic, and educational experience, encouraging scientific curiosity and making knowledge about the universe more accessible to everyone.
details:
QSPHEREx Explorer is a public web tool that lets anyone discover moving objects in the sky, such as asteroids, comets, brown dwarfs, and variable stars.

The user enters the coordinates of a sky region (RA and Dec) and the tool shows that same region at different times, as a blink-style video animation. When played, the moving point of light is easy to spot, while fixed stars stay still.

It includes play, pause, and speed controls, image add / subtract modes to highlight motion, quick-test buttons for objects like Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, and WISE 0855, and a shareable URL with the coordinates.

Its benefit is to democratize astronomical discovery: it turns the more than one billion objects observed by NASA's SPHEREx mission into a simple, visual task that students and the general public can do, without needing to be astronomers or know how to code.

It was built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web viewer, Python and Jupyter for data processing, and open data from NASA/IPAC, SPHEREx, and Gaia DR3. Its creativity is in turning 102 bands of infrared light into a “video of the sky” experience where the human eye detects motion. The team focused on accessibility, easy updates with new SPHEREx data, and the use of verifiable data.
